mainTopic: Proving against the בייתוסים that שבועות does not always fall on a Sunday
overview: This amud continues the argument with the בייתוסים, who said the count to שבועות must always start after a regular שבת, so שבועות would always fall on a Sunday. First רבן יוחנן בן זכאי knocks down an elderly בייתוסי's 'love of Israel' argument. Then he brings a real proof: one פסוק says 'fifty days' and another says 'seven complete weeks,' and complete weeks happen only when פסח begins on שבת. Next comes a memory list. After it, רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע, רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהודה בן בתירא each bring their own proof that 'ממחרת השבת' means the day after the first day of פסח. A ברייתא then teaches that every single person must count the עומר. In the same ברייתא, רבי יוסי בר יהודה proves from the fixed number of fifty days that the count cannot depend on the weekly שבת. The amud ends with רבי יהודה בן בתירא saying that proof is not needed. His own proof comes on the next amud.

steps.title: If משה loved Israel, why did they wander forty years?
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי turns the בייתוסי's 'love of Israel' argument against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if משה רבינו really loved the Jewish people, why did he keep them in the desert for forty years?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי is pushing back on the old man's claim. The old man had said משה made שבועות fall on Sunday out of love, so the people would get two days of rest in a row.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old man's argument was only a guess about what משה would have wanted. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי shows that this kind of reasoning proves nothing. By the same logic, a loving משה would never have let the people wander for forty years, yet they did.

keyTerms.meaning: a lover of the Jewish people

phrases.english: why did he delay them in the wilderness
phrases.notes: 'He' is משה. This answers the old man's claim that משה set שבועות on Sunday out of love, to give the people a two-day rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ אוֹהֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the rebuttal of the בייתוסי argument from the previous part of the daf.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the בייתוסי reasoning that משה's love proves שבועות must fall on Sunday.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Guessing what a loving משה would have wanted cannot decide the law. The forty years of wandering show this.

steps.title: The old man complains that this is a brush-off
steps.stepSummary: The בייתוסי objects that a clever retort is not a real proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: The old man said: My teacher, you're getting rid of me with that?
steps.whatsHappening: The old man protests that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי only answered him with a comeback. He wants a real source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old man has a point. Showing that his argument is weak does not prove the opposite position. This complaint sets up the next move, where a real proof from the תורה will be given.

keyTerms.meaning: you dismiss me / send me away

phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to the rebuttal in step 1 as not being a real proof.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Weakening the other side's argument does not give a positive source for your own view.

steps.title: Our תורה can surely answer your idle talk
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי promises a real proof from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Fool! Shouldn't our complete תורה be at least as good as your empty chatter?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי agrees to bring a real proof. He is setting up the proof from the פסוקים that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He means that the old man's argument was just idle talk. If a comeback was enough to answer it, then the תורה itself will certainly give a full answer. The next step brings that proof.

phrases.english: And shall our perfect Torah not be

phrases.notes: He means: your argument was only empty talk, so our תורה can surely give an answer at least as strong.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹטֶה! וְלֹא תְּהֵא תּוֹרָה שְׁלֵמָה שֶׁלָּנוּ כְּשִׂיחָה בְּטֵילָה שֶׁלָּכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the complaint in step 2 and promises a real proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real source, not just a comeback.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A proof from the תורה will be given, and it follows in the next steps.

steps.title: Two verses: fifty days or seven complete weeks
steps.stepSummary: Two פסוקים about the count to שבועות seem to contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: One פסוק says, 'You shall count fifty days,' and another פסוק says, 'There shall be seven complete weeks.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי points out two פסוקים that seem to clash. This sets up a contradiction that will be resolved in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Seven complete weeks' sounds like full Sunday-to-שבת weeks. 'Fifty days' sounds like a simple count of days, whatever day of the week it starts on. Both must be true somehow, and the way they fit together will become the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: one verse says... and another verse says (two verses that seem to contradict)

phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:16
ויקרא 23:15

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the real proof promised in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the count to שבועות does not have to start on a Sunday

steps.title: Complete weeks only when פסח falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: Each פסוק describes a different kind of year, which shows that שבועות is not always on Sunday.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do the two fit together? One פסוק is talking about a year when the first day of פסח falls on שבת. The other is talking about a year when it falls in the middle of the week.
steps.whatsHappening: The contradiction is resolved by applying each פסוק to a different calendar situation. This finishes the proof against the בייתוסים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first day of פסח is on שבת, the count starts on Sunday, and you get seven complete Sunday-to-שבת weeks. If it falls midweek, the weeks are not calendar weeks, so you just count fifty days. The fifty-day פסוק only makes sense if the count can start on a weekday, so the count does not always begin on Sunday.

keyTerms.meaning: how so? How do these fit together?
the festival (here: the first day of פסח)

steps.whatToRemember: 'Seven complete weeks' fits only a year when פסח begins on שבת. 'Fifty days' covers the other years. So the count, and שבועות, is not tied to Sunday, against the בייתוסים.
steps.confusionAlert: In this step, 'שבת' in 'אמצע שבת' means 'week,' not the day of rest. Also, 'יום טוב' here means the first day of פסח, not שבועות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This supports the חכמים's reading that 'ממחרת השבת' means the day after the first day of פסח. That reading is the basis for how ספירת העומר is counted in practice.

phrases.notes: The festival here is the first day of פסח. The count begins on the day after it.

phrases.english: falls in the middle of the week.
phrases.notes: Here 'שבת' means the week, not the day of rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 4, and that resolution completes the proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each verse applies to a different case (different calendar years).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to clash, since 'complete weeks' suggests a Sunday start.
steps.terutzMaskana: Complete weeks happen only when פסח falls on שבת. Otherwise you count fifty days, so the count can begin midweek.

steps.title: Memory list for more proofs
steps.stepSummary: A memory aid listing further proofs against the בייתוסים from four sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: רבי אליעזר — 'number'; רבי יהושע — 'count'; רבי ישמעאל — 'עומר'; רבי יהודה — 'below.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a memory list for the proofs that are coming next. This is a setup line that previews the next part of the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each key word hints at the proof one sage will bring for the same point. The list itself proves nothing yet. It only helps the learner keep track of the four proofs that follow.

phrases.notes: This is a memory list: each word hints at one sage's proof that's coming up. Some versions have these words and some don't.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof is complete, the גמרא introduces a list of further proofs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four more sages each bring a proof against the בייתוסים, listed here by key words.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: The count depends on the court
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר proves from the words 'count for yourself' that the counting depends on the בית דין, so השבת must mean יום טוב and not the weekly שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: You don't need that proof. The פסוק says 'count for yourself.' That means the counting depends on the בית דין, because they are the ones who set the months. So 'the day after השבת' means the day after יום טוב. That rules out the regular weekly שבת, which anyone can count to on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives his own proof against the בייתוסים. He says the counting is tied to the בית דין, so it must start from יום טוב, whose date the בית דין sets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weekly שבת comes every seven days, so anyone can count to it without help from anyone. A יום טוב depends on when the בית דין declared the new month. Since the תורה ties the count to the בית דין, the starting point must be יום טוב, not the weekly שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Counting (here, counting the days and weeks to שבועות)
To set the new month (declare ראש חודש)
'From the day after השבת', the פסוק everyone is arguing about
The regular weekly שבת, which is fixed from Creation

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: It is not needed,
phrases.notes: He means there's no need for the earlier proof from the two פסוקים. He has a simpler one.

phrases.english: for it says: "You shall count for yourself,"
phrases.notes: דברים 16:9

phrases.english: the counting depends on the court,
since they know how to set the new month.
"From the day after the Shabbat" means the day after the Festival,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:15

phrases.english: which rules out the weekly Shabbat of Creation,
whose counting can be done by any person.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי אליעזר אומר: אינו צריך, הרי הוא אומר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First of the further proofs listed in the memory aid. It sets aside the earlier proof and offers a simpler one.
steps.raayaObject: That ממחרת השבת means the day after the first day of פסח, not the day after the weekly שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word לך in 'תספר לך' (דברים 16:9) shows the counting depends on the בית דין

steps.title: רבי יהושע: Counting to שבועות is like counting to the new month
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע compares counting to שבועות with counting to ראש חודש. In both, the starting point is known ahead of time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: The תורה said to count days and then make the new month holy, and also to count days and then make שבועות holy. Just as with the month you know ahead of time where the count starts, so too with שבועות you know ahead of time where the count starts.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע brings a second proof by comparing two kinds of counting in the תורה: counting toward ראש חודש and counting toward שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting toward the next month always starts on a fixed day, the first of the month. Since the תורה treats the count to שבועות the same way, its starting point must also be a fixed date. That fixed date is the day after the first day of פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: And make holy (by bringing the special קרבנות)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: The Torah said
count days and sanctify the month,
Just as the month is known close to its coming,
phrases.notes: He means you know ahead of time where the count toward the new month begins.

phrases.english: so too Shavuot is known close to its coming.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יהושע אומר: אמרה תורה מנה ימים וקדש חדש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate proof from the memory aid list, using a comparison instead of a word in the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That the count to שבועות starts from a fixed date (the day after the first day of פסח)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The comparison between counting days to ראש חודש and counting days to שבועות

steps.title: Why the בייתוסים' view breaks the comparison
steps.stepSummary: If שבועות were always the day after שבת, its count would not start from a fixed, known date.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say שבועות is always after שבת, how could it be known from what comes before it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how רבי יהושע's comparison knocks down the בייתוסים' view. It challenges them with a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the count always started on a Sunday, its starting date would move around each year. Then the start of the count could not be known from a fixed date the way the count to ראש חודש is. So the comparison only works if the count starts on a fixed date after פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (bringing up the other side's view in order to reject it)

phrases.notes: This is the בייתוסים' view: שבועות always falls on a Sunday.

phrases.english: how will it be known from what is before it?

steps.triggerLanguage: ואם תאמר: עצרת לעולם אחר השבת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יהושע's argument by showing how his comparison clashes with the בייתוסים' view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The בייתוסים' claim that שבועות always falls on Sunday
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the count always started on a Sunday, it would have no fixed starting date. That breaks the comparison to counting toward ראש חודש.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: The עומר must be brought at the start of the festival
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל compares the עומר on פסח to the שתי הלחם on שבועות. Both must be brought at the start of the festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: The תורה said to bring the עומר on פסח and the שתי הלחם on שבועות. Just as there (שבועות) it is the festival and the start of the festival, so too here (פסח) it must be the festival and the start of the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל gives another proof by comparing the עומר offering on פסח to the שתי הלחם offering on שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבועות is only one day long, so the שתי הלחם are always brought at the very start of the festival. By comparison, the עומר must also come at the start of פסח. If the עומר always waited for Sunday, it could fall near the end of פסח, which breaks the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on פסח, which starts the count
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות

steps.whatToRemember: Each sage brings a different proof, but they all reach the same point: the count starts from a fixed date tied to פסח, the day after the first day of יום טוב, and not always on a Sunday.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says: The Torah said
and the two loaves on Shavuot.
Just as there, it is the festival and the start of the festival,
phrases.notes: 'There' means שבועות. It is only one day long, so the loaves are always brought right at its start.

phrases.english: so too here, it is the festival and the start of the festival.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means פסח and the עומר.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי ישמעאל אומר: אמרה תורה הבא עומר בפסח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third separate proof from the memory aid list, this time from the timing of the offerings.
steps.raayaObject: That the עומר is brought at the start of פסח, not on whatever Sunday falls during the week
steps.raayaSupportSource: The comparison between the עומר on פסח and the שתי הלחם on שבועות

steps.title: The word שבת above and below
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא compares the word שבת in the start-of-counting פסוק with the word שבת in the end-of-counting פסוק. In the second פסוק it leads right into a festival, so in the first פסוק it must lead right out of a festival too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: The word 'שבת' is written above, and the word 'שבת' is written below. Just as there it is about a festival, and the start of the festival comes right next to it, so too here it is about a festival, and it comes right next to the start of the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן בתירא gives the fourth proof from the memory list. He learns the meaning of שבת in one פסוק from its meaning in the next פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the 'below' פסוק (ממחרת השבת השביעית), the day after that שבת is שבועות itself, so the festival starts right next to it. So in the 'above' פסוק, ממחרת השבת must also be right next to the start of a festival: the day after the first day of פסח. According to the בייתוסים, the count could start days after פסח begins, which breaks the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Above / below: the earlier פסוק and the later פסוק in the same section
A festival (one of the pilgrimage holidays)
Right next to it, with no gap

phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:15, where the counting begins.
ויקרא 23:16, where the counting ends and שבועות arrives.

phrases.english: Just as there, it is a festival,
and the beginning of the festival is right next to it,
so too here, it is a festival,
and the beginning of the festival is right next to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth separate proof from the memory list, after רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע, and רבי ישמעאל. Each proof reaches the same conclusion independently.
steps.raayaObject: That השבת in ממחרת השבת means the first day of פסח
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison between the word שבת in ויקרא 23:15 and in ויקרא 23:16

steps.title: Every person must count
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'וספרתם לכם' that counting the עומר is a duty for each individual, not just for the community.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: 'And you shall count for yourselves' means that there must be a counting for each and every person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the counting. Its first line teaches who must count: every single person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לכם ('for yourselves') shows the counting is personal. It is not enough for the בית דין or the community to count once for everyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that every Jew counts ספירת העומר personally, not only the community.

phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:15

phrases.english: that there should be a counting for each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about the counting, after the list of proofs ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Counting the עומר is an obligation on each individual.

steps.title: Which שבת does the תורה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: does ממחרת השבת mean the day after the first day of פסח, or the day after the regular weekly שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From the day after the שבת' means from the day after the festival. Or maybe it only means the day after the weekly שבת of Creation?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets up a question about the meaning of השבת. This is preparing the next move, where רבי יוסי בר יהודה will prove the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first states its view (the day after יום טוב), then raises the other possible reading: the regular Saturday. That second reading is the view of the בייתוסים, and the next step will knock it down.

keyTerms.meaning: The weekly שבת, the day of rest from Creation
'Or maybe it only means': a formula raising another possible reading
From the day after the festival (the first day of פסח)

phrases.english: from the day after the festival,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְמָחֳרַת שַׁבַּת בְּרֵאשִׁית?
phrases.english: or is it only the day after the Shabbat of Creation?
phrases.notes: He means the regular weekly Saturday, so the count would always begin on a Sunday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְמָחֳרַת שַׁבַּת בְּרֵאשִׁית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same ברייתא moves on to the next words of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether השבת means the first day of פסח or the weekly שבת

steps.title: The count is always exactly fifty days
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה proves from 'תספרו חמשים יום' that the counting must always come out to exactly fifty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: The פסוק says 'you shall count fifty days.' All the counting that you count must be only fifty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר יהודה answers the question by pointing to the number fifty in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה gives a fixed number: fifty days. So the count must always run fifty days from a fixed point in פסח. The next step shows why the weekly-שבת reading breaks this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Look, it says': pointing to a פסוק as proof

phrases.english: it says: "you shall count fifty days",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:16

phrases.english: all the countings that you count

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: That השבת means the first day of פסח
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fixed number 'fifty days' in ויקרא 23:16

steps.title: The weekly-שבת reading gives a changing number
steps.stepSummary: If the count began after the weekly שבת, the number of days from פסח to שבועות would change every year, from fifty-one up to fifty-six.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it means the day after the weekly שבת, sometimes you will find fifty-one days, and sometimes fifty-two, fifty-three, fifty-four, fifty-five, or fifty-six.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר יהודה finishes his proof by showing the problem with the בייתוסים' reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח falls on a different weekday each year. If the count waits for the next Sunday, the gap from פסח to שבועות grows by up to six extra days. That clashes with the תורה's fixed 'fifty days', so השבת must mean the first day of פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you say': introducing the other view in order to show its problem

steps.whatToRemember: Two proofs here against the בייתוסים: the word שבת compared above and below (רבי יהודה בן בתירא), and the fixed fifty days (רבי יוסי בר יהודה). Also, every person must count the עומר.

phrases.english: And if you say from the day after the Shabbat of Creation,

phrases.notes: Counting from the day after the first day of פסח, the gap would grow depending on which weekday פסח fell on.

phrases.english: and sometimes you will find fifty-two,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out why the fifty-day rule from the previous step rules out the weekly-שבת reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that ממחרת השבת means the day after the weekly שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading makes the time from פסח to שבועות change each year, while the תורה fixes it at fifty days.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says the earlier proof is not needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says the proof just brought is unnecessary. He is about to offer a different way to prove the same point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: That proof is not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן בתירא, the same תנא quoted in step 11, says we don't need the previous proof about the count always coming out to fifty days. The גמרא is setting up the next move, where he brings his own proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees with the conclusion that ממחרת השבת means the day after the first day of פסח. He only says the long fifty-day argument isn't needed to get there. His own proof is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed. Used when a sage says a proof or source is unnecessary because there is an easier way to show the same thing.

steps.confusionAlert: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ does not mean the earlier proof is wrong. It means that proof is not needed, because there is an easier way to reach the same conclusion.

phrases.notes: He means the proof רבי יוסי בר יהודה just gave, that the count must always come out to fifty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the proof of רבי יוסי בר יהודה (Steps 14-15) by saying it is unnecessary. This opens an alternative proof for the same conclusion.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the need for the fifty-day proof, not its correctness or its conclusion.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No flaw in the logic is claimed. The proof is simply more than is needed, because a more direct source is available.
